title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A student chats with your makerspace assistant on Monday. The program stores nothing when the session ends. On Tuesday the same student starts a new session. What does the context of the first model call on Tuesday hold?

options.text: A summary of Monday that the model wrote and kept itself
The system prompt, the tools and the new question only
Monday's messages, which the model keeps for about a day
The student's last ten messages, held by the model itself

items.stem: In one request, the system prompt and tool definitions take 2,000 tokens and the student's question takes 100 tokens. The model is called three times: it requests a tool, then requests a second tool, then writes the final answer. Each tool request is 50 tokens and each tool result is 500 tokens, and every call re-sends the full earlier context. Counting only the input of the three calls (not the final answer), how many tokens does the model read in total?

Your check_calendar tool returns a machine's whole year of bookings, about 20,000 tokens, when the model needs only tomorrow's free slots. In an agent that makes several model calls per request, why is this a bigger problem than in a single model call?

options.text: The model deletes older results by itself, so facts get lost
A tool result can be read by the model only one time
Every later call re-sends the result, so you pay for it again
Long results make the program stop, since tools have size limits

items.stem: Your team could save "student passed the laser cutter course" as a note after a session, or the assistant could ask a training-record tool each time. In one or two sentences, why is asking the tool the safer design for this fact?

A student asks about replacing the laser cutter's lens, and the assistant retrieves a page from a 120-page manual. In one or two sentences, what does the program do to retrieve it, and where does the page end up so that the model can use it?
